Description: Inventory the estate, agree a strategy and owner per workload, and group workloads into waves by dependency cluster. Exit criteria: every workload has an owner, a strategy, a wave and a recorded dependency set.
Account structure, three-tier VPC, hybrid connectivity and guardrails. Exit criteria: terraform apply reproduces the landing zone from empty and hybrid connectivity is tested at real throughput.

EKS, ECS Fargate and the EC2 rehost target, plus the CI/CD pipeline that deploys to them. Exit criteria: a commit reaches staging automatically and a rollback has been performed deliberately and timed.
Move workloads wave by wave: build, replicate, test, cut over, validate. Exit criteria: every workload in the wave is validated and its source is decommissioned or formally retained.
Hypercare, right-sizing against real demand, cost controls and operational handover. Exit criteria: workloads are owned by the run team with runbooks, dashboards and alarms in place.

Summary: Run Application Discovery Service across the estate
Description: Collect utilisation and dependency data. Right-size from real metrics rather than replicating existing over-provisioning.

Summary: Identify retirement candidates and confirm with owners
Description: Typically 10-20% of an estate has no real consumers. Confirm with owners, not logs alone - a quiet service is not necessarily an unused one.

Summary: Assign a strategy, owner and wave to every workload
Description: Record in the tracker, not a spreadsheet. Waves are grouped by dependency cluster, never by team convenience.
Undiscovered dependencies are the most common cause of cutover overrun. Use flow data, and keep wave 1 low-criticality.

Summary: Agree the IPAM plan with the network team
Description:
Allocate non-overlapping CIDRs for every environment before any VPC is
built. Overlap found after Direct Connect is live costs weeks.

Summary: Order Direct Connect and stand up backup VPN
Description: DX lead time is 6-12 weeks and sits on the critical path. VPN carries the early waves.

Summary: Build the three-tier VPC with Terraform
Description:
Public, private and isolated data subnets across three AZs, with flow
logs and VPC endpoints.

Summary: Provision EKS with IRSA and access entries
Description: Private API endpoint, envelope encryption, managed addons, no cluster-admin by default.

Launch template, ASG behind an internal ALB, SSM Session Manager instead
of SSH, encrypted EBS.
Isolated data subnets, credentials generated into Secrets Manager, forced TLS.
No static AWS keys. Trust policies pin the exact subject claim per environment.

Summary: Build the CI pipeline with a coverage gate
Description: Parallel lint, type, unit and integration jobs with an 80% floor and a regression gate.

Deliberately fail a rollout and time the automatic rollback. An untested
rollback is a hypothesis.

Summary: Run two weeks of hypercare per wave
Description: Migration engineers stay on the rota. Do not hand straight to a run team that has never seen the workload.

Summary: Right-size workloads after two weeks of data
Description: Deliberately deferred so cutover changes one variable, not two. Use CloudWatch and Compute Optimizer against real demand.

Summary: Purchase Savings Plans once usage stabilises
Description: Committing during migration locks in the pre-optimisation shape.

Summary: Hand over runbooks, dashboards and alarms
Description: Operational transfer per workload, with alarms landing on the shared SNS topic used by the pipeline.

Summary: Decommission source systems after the retention window
Description: Sources are retained read-only for the agreed period, then removed.
